Purpose and exclusions

A minimal party/eligibility contract is needed before group combat rewards; full invite/leave/leader UI arrives in Phase 19. Party membership is a versioned social record, not a list invented independently by each zone server.

Never bypass the declared rule owner, mutate an authored definition at runtime, trust a client completion claim, or infer a compiled implementation from this page.

Creation and configuration

  1. Create PartyPolicy and DB_party_memberships/DB_party_memberships/DB_party_memberships records before group rewards. Seed Party_AB in the development service at Phase 08.
  2. Create WBP_Party with name/class/health/presence indicators, invite response, leave and leader controls; advanced UI integration is explicitly Phase 19.
  3. Reopen encounter and quest rules to use membership revision plus deliberate eligibility, not all nearby actors.
  4. Reopen dungeon allocator to reserve a coherent party roster, and chat routing to use authenticated party membership.
  5. Test cross-zone presence and one disconnected member without leaking private inventory or making a stale Actor pointer authoritative.

Required sequence: create native prerequisites -> actual build -> child/data creation -> configure -> assign to listed consumer -> save -> run named fixture. A compiled shell without its consumer assignment is not feature completion.

Lifecycle and cleanup

  1. Construct with only safe defaults; no service calls or world scans from construction scripts.
  2. Inject current owner/definition/session and subscribe once after readiness. Possession and replicated state may arrive in either order; guard initialization.
  3. Accept only permitted commands under current identity/epoch; keep local UI/cosmetic prediction separate from committed state.
  4. After server/backend result apply only matching request generation and nonstale revision; late reply to old body does not mutate new body.
  5. On death, transfer, disconnect, restart or teardown cancel transient work, clear input/timers, unbind delegates and release weak observers. Durable receipts remain authoritative.
  6. On reconnect create fresh runtime objects from current committed snapshot; never deserialize old Actor/widget pointers or rerun initial grants.

Concrete player-to-authority flow

Participation in Parties, invitations, group credit and leadership. Rule owner: URPGPartyComponent. This asset’s role is A minimal party/eligibility contract is needed before group combat rewards; full invite/leave/leader UI arrives in Phase 19. Party membership is a versioned social record, not a list invented independently by each zone server.

  1. Phase 08 uses a service-created Party_AB fixture with two authenticated members; no public invitation UI is required for Slice A.
  2. In Phase 19 inviter selects an identity, server/backend validates block/membership/capacity and stores a short-lived invitation.
  3. Invitee accepts using their own authenticated session; backend atomically updates party membership/revision and invitation state.
  4. Zone servers receive safe membership/presence projections; party UI binds by CharacterId and resolves currently relevant actor pointers transiently.
  5. Combat/quest/dungeon systems snapshot eligible party members under their own proximity/contribution/share policies; joining after defeat does not retroactively obtain loot.
  6. Leave/disband/leader disconnect follows deterministic succession policy and invalidates stale pending instance reservations as required.

Named fixture and acceptance

Fixture: L_Rillmere / Party_AB / Character_A / Character_B. Configure this asset at its first phase and run the linked phase recipe. Actual result: not run in Unreal/backend during documentation generation.

Stimulus / expected result
Two invitations accepted into different parties concurrently -> membership uniqueness allows one valid result.
Party fills before accept -> PartyFull.
Blocked player invites -> Blocked with privacy-safe response.
Leader disconnects -> declared succession after grace, not a permanently unusable party.

Record expected/observed separately. Reopen the concrete map consumer; inspect authoritative state, stable IDs/revisions and UI. Static link checks cannot satisfy this gameplay test.

Common mistakes and staged limits

Do not duplicate a native rule in Blueprint, assume a planned type is compiled, or keep callbacks/owners valid after world or session replacement.

Do not build later references as empty shells in an earlier phase. Source-derived art rows remain blocked by the missing ZIP; plugin API bindings remain blocked by installed-source verification. Placeholder visuals and proposed tuning are explicitly not production proof.
